_help: Per commodity, an indicator->1-5 map (5 = bullish). A bare number or {"score": n, "note": "why"} for auditability. Unset = held at neutral and excluded from the average, exactly like fundamentals_manual. Refreshed by the fx-strength-desk-daily task, step 2c.

Real yield direction.note: Still a headwind: the 10-year eased only to ~4.84-4.86% (10 Sep) near the highest since 2023, and August PPI printed hot at +0.4% m/m / +5.4% y/y (a tenth above forecast, energy +4.2% on the US-Iran conflict), which keeps a term-premium/inflation lift on yields on top of a ~57-63% September Fed hike bet. 11 Sep CPI and the 16 Sep FOMC are the swing factors.

US dollar direction.note: DXY around the high-98s (from the 99.39 post-payrolls high). Hot PPI on 10 Sep gives the dollar a mild firming bias into CPI/FOMC, but the September hike is largely priced and oil-driven risk aversion caps the bid. Roughly neutral for gold.

Central-bank & ETF demand.note: Both legs now pulling the same way. WGC data: global gold ETFs added US$18bn in August (second-largest monthly inflow on record) and Q3 is the strongest quarter on record - the Western-outflow risk flagged on 6 Sep has clearly reversed, inflows are running hard through the hawkish-Fed repricing. Central banks still accumulating above official net-purchase reports; 2026 sell-side targets ($4,900-6,000 year-end) rest on continued official buying. Not a 5 only because gold is at record highs and chasing here carries drawdown risk.

Safe-haven bid.note: Still escalating - no ceasefire, US-Iran Strait of Hormuz tensions ongoing (attacks on shipping, a proposed transit-toll system), Brent holding around/above $100. Gold is holding near its record ~$4,400 despite a ~4.85% 10-year, i.e. the haven bid is offsetting the rates drag rather than being overwhelmed by it.

Real yield direction.note: Same headwind as gold - 10-year ~4.84-4.86% (10 Sep), hot August PPI (+5.4% y/y), ~57-63% September Fed hike priced into the 16 Sep FOMC. Silver is more leveraged to the move, so the drag is felt at least as much here. 11 Sep CPI is the swing factor.

US dollar direction.note: DXY in the high-98s; hot PPI gives a mild dollar-firming bias into CPI/FOMC but the hike is largely priced. Roughly neutral for silver.

Industrial demand.note: Structural solar/electronics/AI-datacentre demand stays firm and silver is tracking the metals bid, but 2026 global growth is slowing (IEA has oil demand contracting on trade disruption), which caps the cyclical industrial pull. Net mildly positive, unchanged.

Gold-silver ratio.note: Ratio ~65 (XAU ~4470 / XAG ~68.4), compressed further from ~67.5 a week ago and well below the long-run ~80 average - silver has already closed most of the gap to gold and is no longer cheap on this measure. Neutral for further silver outperformance.

OPEC+ supply policy.note: On 6 Sep the seven core OPEC+ members PAUSED output increases, holding October quotas at the September level (31.01 Mb/d) after four straight monthly hikes - members want to set 2027 baselines first and the Hormuz disruption has cut the group's ability to move price anyway. Removes the 'more barrels coming' overhang for Q4; supportive, though widely expected. Next meeting 4 Oct.

Inventory trend.note: API reported a small crude draw (~-0.3 Mb) for the week ending 4 Sep; the EIA weekly report was pushed to 12:00/14:00 ET on 10 Sep by the 7 Sep federal closure. The mid-August build had already fully reversed and EIA's STEO expects stocks near/below the 5-year low through year-end on strong exports and low imports. August PPI energy +4.2% underlines the tight physical picture. Slightly tight.

Demand outlook.note: Still the August IEA Oil Market Report read: 2026 demand contracting (~-80 kb/d), sharpest quarterly drop since Covid, as trade disruption hits advanced economies, Asia and the Middle East. Nothing since has reversed it - current price strength is entirely the Hormuz supply-risk premium, not demand. Next IEA OMR due mid-September.

Geopolitical risk premium.note: Still elevated and escalating: US-Iran Strait of Hormuz tensions ongoing with no ceasefire signal, attacks on shipping and a proposed transit-toll regime, Brent around/above $100 (WTI ~$96). Holding at 4.5 - already near the top of the range.
